claims_assessed.detail: Version 2.0.0 confirmed on CRAN. Release date is 2025-06-30 per CRAN index page; NEWS.md shows release date as June 26, 2025. Minor discrepancy (June 26 vs June 30) - one is authoring date, one is CRAN publication date. Effectively verified.

claims_assessed.claim: Rmonize uses two coordinated tables: DataSchema and DPE (Data Processing Elements)
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed. CRAN description and documentation explicitly describe DataSchema (target variable definitions) and Data Processing Elements (one row per DataSchema variable per input dataset).

claims_assessed.claim: Rmonize has an 8-type enum for rule types: direct_mapping, recode, case_when, operation, other, impossible, undetermined, id_creation
claims_assessed.detail: Rmonize's DPE has a 'rule_category' column (NOT 'rule_type') with 9 values, not 8: id_creation, direct_mapping, recode, case_when, paste, operation, other, impossible, undetermined. The skeptic pass omits 'paste' from the list. The column name is 'rule_category', not 'rule_type'. The count is 9, not 8.
Version 0.3.6 confirmed on CRAN with publication date 2025-10-16.

psHarmonize's harmonization sheet (code_type column) has exactly 2 modification types: 'recode category' and 'function'. The documentation explicitly states 'There are two different types of modifications you can choose from.' Not 3 types.
Confirmed. The harmonization sheet includes a 'coding_notes' column used for documenting transformation decisions (e.g., 'No change needed', 'Convert from inches to cm').

claims_assessed.claim: retroharmonize v0.2.8, CRAN 2026-05-21, unstable — archived Jan–May 2026
claims_assessed.detail: Version 0.2.8 confirmed on CRAN, published May 21, 2026. Package was archived on 2026-01-30 (due to dependency on archived 'dataset' package) and restored/re-published May 21, 2026. The characterization 'archived Jan–May 2026' is accurate.

claims_assessed.claim: retroharmonize takes a programmatic/metadata-object approach for ex-post survey harmonization from DDI/SPSS sources
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed from CRAN description and package documentation. Uses comprehensive S3 classes. DDI/SPSS source handling is part of its design.

claims_assessed.claim: Opal uses server-side JavaScript-based derived variables
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed. Opal uses the Magma JavaScript API (via Rhino JS engine) for derived variables. 'A derived variable is a variable which values are computed using a script that is expressed using the Magma Javascript API.'

claims_assessed.claim: Opal has an embedded per-variable VCS with REST API access to full script history
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed via GitHub issue #1816 which explicitly defines REST API endpoints for per-variable VCS: GET commits for a view, GET commits for a specific variable script, GET commit details with diffs, GET script at specific commit blob.

claims_assessed.claim: Rmonize is peer-reviewed (IJE guidelines paper, PMC5407152)
claims_assessed.detail: PMC5407152 is confirmed as the Maelstrom Research guidelines for rigorous retrospective data harmonization, published in IJE 2016. However, this paper describes the *guidelines/methodology*, not Rmonize the R package specifically. Rmonize is the software implementation of those guidelines. The citation is legitimate but the framing 'peer-reviewed (IJE guidelines paper)' conflates the guidelines paper with the R package.

claims_assessed.claim: The Maelstrom five processing-model taxonomy includes: algorithmic transformation, calibration, standardization, latent variable, imputation
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed from Maelstrom Research data-processing-methods page. The five models are: (1) Algorithmic Transformation, (2) Simple Calibration Model, (3) Standardization Model, (4) Latent Variable Model, (5) Multiple Imputation Models.

claims_assessed.claim: PMC5837212 is Opal/Mica paper in IJE
claims_assessed.detail: PMC5837212 is confirmed as the Opal and Mica software profile paper published in International Journal of Epidemiology (2017).

claims_assessed.claim: Rmonize embeds R code directly in DPE cells for recode, case_when, and operation rules
claims_assessed.detail: Confirmed. The DPE algorithm column contains R code expressions directly in cells.
arxiv 2411.10342v1 describes an EHRs Data Harmonization Platform built on recodeflow (a Shiny app). It is NOT about retroharmonize, though it mentions retroharmonize as a related tool.
